navi — synchronous entry point.

import navi let api = newNavi() let res = api.get("http://example.com") echo res.status, " ", res.body

For async, import navi/asyncdispatch or navi/chronos instead (exactly one entry module per program).

Verb sugar shared by every entry module via include.

Not a standalone module: it is included after the including entry module defines Navi and request. The auto return type adapts to the backend (Response for the sync entry, FutureResponse for the async ones), so this one definition serves all three.

params is generic so a verb accepts any query form -- a seq/array of pairs (@[...], @{...}, {...}) or a Table / OrderedTable -- normalized by toQuery. The typed default keeps the no-params call unambiguous.

Types

Navi = ref object
  pool*: Pool[PooledConn[Conn]]
  jar*: CookieJar
NaviConfig {.requiresInit.} = object of NaviConfigBase
  middleware*: seq[NaviMiddleware]
requiresInit, so it cannot be built with a bare/partial NaviConfig(...) (which would leave fields zeroed, e.g. verify off). Build it with initNaviConfig(). 
NaviContext = ref object
  req*: Request              ## the outgoing request; modify it before `next`
  res*: Response             ## the response; set by `next`, adjust it after
Carried through the middleware chain. A middleware reads and mutates it, then calls next to run the rest of the chain (which fills res). 
NaviMiddleware = proc (ctx: NaviContext) {.closure.}
A middleware step: read/modify ctx.req, call ctx.next() to proceed -- or skip it to short-circuit -- then read/modify ctx.res. Run in order; index 0 is the outermost. A closure, so it can capture: write a factory proc bearer(token: string): NaviMiddleware that returns a step closing over token. 
WebSocket = ref object

proc client(ctx: NaviContext): Navi {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
The client handling this request (e.g. to read ctx.client.config). 
proc close(client: Navi) {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Close all idle pooled connections, freeing their TLS contexts and cached sessions. Optional but recommended when done with a client: a later request just opens fresh connections. Without it, pooled connections are reclaimed only at process exit (and their OpenSSL contexts leak until then). 
proc close(ws: WebSocket; code = closeNormal; reason = "") {....raises: [],
    tags: [RootEffect], forbids: [].}
Send a close frame and close the transport (freeing its TLS context). Idempotent: a no-op once the socket is already closed. 
proc config(client: Navi): lent NaviConfig {....raises: [], tags: [], forbids: [].}
Read-only view of the client's config. Config is fixed at construction; build a fresh client (or extend) to change it rather than mutating a live one, so its pooled connections stay consistent with its settings.

The only way to build a config: NaviConfig requires every field. Sets the safe defaults (verify on, decompress on, 2 retries, 20 redirects); override the fields you want, then pass it to newNavi.

proc parallel(client: Navi; targets: openArray[string]): seq[Response] {....raises: [
    RequestCancelledError, CatchableError, ResponseTooLargeError, Exception,
    ValueError, KeyError], tags: [RootEffect, TimeEffect], forbids: [].}

Fetch many URLs (GET) concurrently. Same-origin requests are multiplexed over one HTTP/2 connection when the server supports h2, otherwise run sequentially, each through the policy layer (cookies, decompression, redirects, retries). Non-2xx responses are returned (not raised) so every result is available; inspect .ok.

When middleware is configured it wraps each request individually, which forgoes the shared-connection multiplexing (every request stands alone).

Perform a request and return the response. json/form/multipart encode the body; bodyStream uploads a chunked body from a pull-based producer. params are appended to the URL query; cancel aborts the request. Configured middleware wraps the whole call.

            cancel: CancelToken = nil): Response {....raises: [
    RequestCancelledError, HttpError, CatchableError, ResponseTooLargeError,
    Exception], tags: [RootEffect, TimeEffect], forbids: [].}
Perform a request and deliver the response body to sink as it arrives. The returned Response carries status and headers but an empty body. 
proc websocket(client: Navi; url: string; headers = initHeaders()): WebSocket {.
    ...raises: [Exception, IOError], tags: [RootEffect], forbids: [].}
Open a WebSocket connection (RFC 6455). Accepts ws:// / wss:// (or http/https); wss uses TLS. Does the HTTP/1.1 Upgrade over the transport and validates Sec-WebSocket-Accept. Use send, receive, and close.
